notes: Opens a raw Socket(host,port), sends an HTTP 'CONNECT host:port HTTP/1.0' request (with optional proxy-auth header line), reads the response status line: returns the socket on 200, on 407 scans headers for 'proxy-authenticate:' and throws IOException_Sub1 with the auth scheme, otherwise closes and returns null. Clear HTTP CONNECT-tunnel implementation.

Overrides SocketFactory's abstract createSocket (see SocketFactory.kt method2050/method2047 - the base class already establishes this as the socket-factory entry point, and DirectSocketFactory's sibling override just delegates straight to method2047). Enables java.net.useSystemProxies, determines whether the target port is 443 (https) to pick which URI scheme to query first, gets candidate proxies from ProxySelector for both schemes, merges them, and tries each via method2053 until one connects; falls back to a direct socket (method2047) on total failure or URI syntax error. `if (i >= -100) return null` at the top is an odd early-out gate - given call sites pass small negative/positive sentinel values (-112 seen at one call site), this looks like an obfuscator opaque-predicate/decoy guard rather than meaningful port validation; flagged as suspicious.

Given one candidate Proxy: returns a direct socket (method2047) if proxy.type()==DIRECT; for HTTP proxies attempts to read pre-emptive proxy auth via reflection (currently entirely commented out/dead - always leaves `string` null) then calls method2052 to tunnel; for SOCKS proxies opens a Socket(proxy) and connects directly. `gateFlag` must equal literal 125 or the method immediately returns null - every call site passes the literal 125.toByte(), so this is a decoy/redundant guard, not a real runtime condition.
